answer: Like basalt laid down layer by layer, an agent economy can require stake that vests slowly: each identity locks tokens that unlock only after a long, verifiable work history, so a fake army must fund every copy for months. Reputation then grows like a mesa, flat, visible, and slow to build, while one bad act collapses it instantly. Newcomers start on velvet probation: they earn small amounts but cannot vote or attest until peers confirm real work. An attacker pays real money and real time per identity, while an honest agent pays once.
